promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Tawhid and the nature of God
The articles of faith and prophethood
Angels, holy books and life after death

questions.q: What does the Arabic term 'Tawhid' mean?
options: The oneness and unity of God
questions.explain: Tawhid is the central Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and unity of Allah.

questions.q: What is the term for the sin of associating anything or anyone as a partner with God?
questions.explain: Shirk, associating partners with Allah, is considered the gravest sin because it denies Tawhid.

questions.q: Muslims believe Allah is 'transcendent'. What does this mean?
options: Allah is beyond and above the created universe
Allah is present within every human heart
questions.explain: Transcendence means Allah exists beyond and independent of the created, physical world.

questions.q: Which term describes the Islamic belief that Allah is all-powerful?
questions.explain: Omnipotence means Allah has unlimited power over all creation.

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses Allah's immanence?
options: Allah is close to and involved with His creation
Allah is entirely separate from the world
Allah is the same as the universe itself
Allah has no knowledge of human affairs
questions.explain: Immanence describes Allah as near to and active within the created world, closer than a person's jugular vein.

questions.q: Traditionally, how many names of Allah are described in Islam, each revealing an aspect of His nature?
questions.explain: The 99 names of Allah, such as Al-Rahman (the Merciful), express His many attributes.

questions.q: How many articles of faith form the foundation of belief in Sunni Islam?
questions.explain: Sunni Islam has six articles of faith, including belief in Tawhid, angels, holy books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and predestination.

questions.q: What is the name for the five roots of religion (Usul ad-Din) in Shia Islam?
options: The five roots of Usul ad-Din
questions.explain: Shia Islam bases belief on the five roots of Usul ad-Din: Tawhid, Adalat, Nubuwwah, Imamah and Mi'ad.

questions.q: Who do Muslims regard as the final prophet and 'Seal of the Prophets'?
questions.explain: Muhammad is believed to be the last prophet, known as Khatam an-Nabiyyin, the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.q: According to Islamic belief, who was the first prophet and the first human being?
questions.explain: Adam is regarded in Islam as both the first human and the first prophet.

questions.q: What does the term 'Risalah' refer to in Islam?
options: Prophethood, the channel of communication between Allah and humanity
The recording of good and bad deeds
questions.explain: Risalah is the belief that Allah communicates His guidance to humanity through chosen prophets.

questions.q: Why is the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) especially significant to Muslims?
options: He rejected idol worship and demonstrated complete submission to Allah
He was the last of the prophets
He was believed to be divine
questions.explain: Ibrahim is honoured for his pure monotheism and willingness to submit fully to Allah's will.

questions.q: A Muslim says all the earlier prophets taught the same core message. Which belief best explains this view?
options: Tawhid, that there is only one God to whom people must submit
Predestination, that everything is decided in advance
Imamah, the leadership of the imams
That every prophet founded a different religion
questions.explain: Muslims believe all prophets from Adam to Muhammad preached the same fundamental message of Tawhid.

questions.q: Which angel revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered Allah's revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

questions.q: According to Islamic teaching, what are angels created from?
questions.explain: Angels are believed to be made from light and, unlike humans, have no free will and always obey Allah.

questions.q: Which angel is known as the angel of death?
questions.explain: Izra'il is the angel of death, responsible for taking souls at the appointed time.

questions.q: Which holy book do Muslims believe was revealed to the prophet Musa (Moses)?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Tawrat was the scripture given by Allah to Musa.

questions.q: Which holy book do Muslims believe was given to the prophet Dawud (David)?
questions.explain: The Zabur, identified with the Psalms, is the scripture Muslims believe was revealed to Dawud.

questions.q: What is 'Akhirah' in Islamic belief?
options: Life after death and the eternal existence of the soul
questions.explain: Akhirah refers to the belief in life after death, when people are judged and sent to paradise or hell.

questions.q: A Muslim tries to act morally throughout life because they believe every deed is recorded and they will one day face Allah. Which belief most directly motivates this?
options: Belief in Yawm al-Din, the Day of Judgement
Belief in the immanence of Allah
Belief in the finality of Muhammad
Belief that angels are made of light
questions.explain: Belief that all will be judged by Allah on the Day of Judgement encourages Muslims to live righteously.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Religious Studies (J625) specification; Islam: Beliefs & Teachings
